data.$comment: ZenSight types shared by several contracts: zs.thresholds.v1 and zs.desired.v1 must agree on ThresholdsConfig, so both list this file unchanged (Gap G12). Faithful to zensight-common/src/threshold.rs, comparison.rs, alert.rs (AlertSeverity) and desired.rs (AppliedConfig).

Ack.description: A write landed. v1 declared Ack without a schema ('ad-hoc JSON on the wire', zensight-common/src/schema.rs:225). In zk2 success is a value reply and failure a reply_err (O3), so nothing but an optional note remains.

AppliedConfig.description: What is actually in force for one reconcilable topic, and why (desired.v1's observed revision: desired_timestamp).

desired_timestamp.description: HLC timestamp of the applied desired sample (source = desired only).

effective_json.description: The document in force, JSON-encoded as a string. Its real type is the topic's.

topic.description: Repeats the key's {topic} (migration debt; tcgui gap 1).

ComparisonOp.description: Serialized in PascalCase (no serde rename); default GreaterThan.

timestamp.description: The rejected sample's HLC timestamp, when it carried one.

clear.description: Value hysteresis, on the quiet side of value.

labels.description: Label globs, all of which must match. v1 proxies matched `source` here; a device service no longer needs to.

metric.description: Glob over the resource path the service publishes (`if/*/in_errors.rate`). Under zk2 the paths change (the device leaves for the service name, rest families move under metrics/), so v1 rule sets need rewriting (migration debt).

name.description: Stable identity; becomes the alarm rule `threshold:<name>`.

ThresholdsConfig.description: The whole rule set one service evaluates, set wholesale (#928, #931). Every field is serde-defaulted.

data.$comment: The historian's request and reply shapes, from zensight-common/src/history.rs and historian.toml. v1 carried the query in selector parameters and named a series (origin, producer, subject). zk2 names it (system, service, interface, resource), the key minus the kind chunk, still derivable from a sample alone. Replies are per series (replies = many), so the per-reply envelope (step_s, partial, covers_from) moves onto each series. RangeReply.historian / TimelineReply.historian go: under O6 a reply rides the operation's concrete key, which names the answering historian.

HistorianError.description: v1 registered error/historian/{range,series,timeline,stats}: a store read failed or a reply could not be encoded. The encoding half is the core `internal`; the store half stays an app detail. A declared-but-unbuilt timeline answers the core `unavailable`, cause build (v1 error/unsupported).

Point.description: (epoch_ms, value), a 2-tuple as serde writes (i64, f64). prefixItems: Gap G12 asks S7 to settle the zk2 subset of JSON Schema.

cursor.description: Opaque value cursor from a previous reply's next_cursor. App-level paging: the core has none (r3.2 U10, §8).

step.description: Seconds, clamped to a tier: <60 the per-second ring, <3600 the minute tier, else the hour tier.

RangeSeries.description: One series' points from one historian, one reply each.

agg.description: The aggregate actually applied, which is not always the one requested.

covers_from.description: RFC 3339; present only when the tier's oldest instant is later than `from`.

next_cursor.description: Present on the last reply of a page that stopped at `limit`. v1 spelled it "<points>:<origin>/<producer>/<subject>" (range.rs:187), a key-shaped cursor; it stays opaque here.

partial.description: The walk stopped before completing this series: limit spent, or the tier could not cover the window (RFC 05 §3.2 marker).

step_s.description: Seconds per point after clamping to a tier.

SeriesSelector.description: Which series. Absent fields match everything; `resource` is a key expression over the resource path (** allowed). v1: ?origin=<h-... or *>;producer=;subject= joined into one pattern (zensight-historian/src/query/range.rs:84-91).

TimelineEntry.description: One occurrence (a trap) or alarm transition, newest first. v1 carried `origin` and the FULL key (history.rs:306-308), and the persisted uid hashed that key string (zensight-store/src/timeline.rs:74-76), so every stored uid changes on migration.
